citation.title: A Geometric-Enhanced Neural Network Method for Scalable and High-Resolution Topology Optimization
citation.authors: Lei Zhang, Shiqiang Li, Zhichu Lei, Guangzhe Du, Xiao Zhang, Guanbin Chen, Wenliang Qian

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: For the simply supported beam, GeNN completed optimization in 32.55 seconds versus 61.36 seconds for SIMP, with a lower reported objective value.
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: 61.36 s / 32.55 s = 1.8851 from section 4.3, Table 1, p. 13.
claim.alternatives: Abstract reports a 256 m bridge with millions of degrees of freedom optimized within ten minutes, without a classical time. Section 4.3, Table 2 compares 3D SIMP and GeNN.

baseline.classical_method: Density-based SIMP with density filtering (section 4 and Table 1)
baseline.implementation: Python 3.10.16 and PyTorch 2.5.1 stated for examples; specific SIMP implementation not stated (section 4)
baseline.solver: 2D solver not stated; 3D linear system uses PARDISO sparse direct solver (section 4.3, p. 14)
baseline.hardware_ml: not stated for Table 1; bridge example used GPU with peak memory about 21.3 GB (section 5, p. 19)
baseline.problem_size: 160 × 80 Q4 elements, 12,800 SIMP design variables for primary SS beam (section 4.3, Table 1, p. 13)
baseline.classical_iterations: 400 iterations for primary SS beam; its stopping rule not stated (Table 1, p. 13)
baseline.classical_time: 61.36 s for primary SS beam (Table 1, p. 13)
baseline.ml_time: 32.55 s for primary SS beam, including per-problem parameter optimization (Table 1, p. 13)
baseline.training_time: 32.55 s per-problem optimization for primary SS beam (Table 1, p. 13); 4× refined inference takes less than 0.02 s after approximately 30 s total training/runtime on separate examples (section 4.2, p. 13)
baseline.data_generation_cost: not applicable; network parameters are optimized anew for each design problem rather than learned from an offline design dataset (section 3, Figure 4)
baseline.quality_gap: GeNN 112,737.99 versus SIMP 115,819.95 objective value for primary SS beam (section 4.3, Table 1, p. 13)

R1.evidence: Section 4.3, Table 1, p. 13: GeNN has lower objective than SIMP under a shared prescribed volume fraction, but SIMP uses 400 iterations with no stated stopping rule or physical-field volume comparison.

R2.evidence: Sections 4 and 4.3, pp. 10 and 13-14: SIMP has a density filter and the 3D solver is PARDISO, but primary 2D solver and hardware are not specified; no article evidence establishes R2(a)-(e).

R3.evidence: Section 3, Figure 4 and section 4.3, Table 1: GeNN parameters are trained within each problem's timed iterative optimization; there is no offline dataset acquisition to amortize.

R4.evidence: Sections 3-4 and Table 1: compliance is computed via FEA on returned density fields and volume is constrained, but infeasible or failed-design rates are not reported.

reporting.n_test_cases: 8 named example types across sections 4-5 (2D cantilever, Michell, L-bracket, SS beam; 3D cantilever; heat, multi-volume, and bridge)

notes: Reporting locators: section 6, Table 6 reports seed stability; sections 4-5 provide selected timings, with no separate hardware assignment for SIMP and GeNN. The Data Availability Statement offers further inquiries; no public source-code link is given. The abstract's bridge time is not a quantitative classical comparison, so the first eligible quantitative comparison is Table 1.
